I’ll add required `DefinitionPlanner` capability to the combined operations trait, with channel-aware dispatch helpers that accept the exact `dyn ChannelAwareProductionDecodeOperations` supplied to session `step`. Then I’ll exercise pattern and group-filter planning through one object, and add the two one-sided opacity publications.

item.aggregated_output:
`FillOpacity` or `StrokeOpacity` (including the initial value `1`) into the
single opacity carried by `PatternMapping`; the channel and mapping remain bound
through `request_mapped` and `complete_mapped` to the final `PatternId` paint.
Both public planner routes share the same owner, source, style, bounds, kind,
mapping, expansion and post validation. Existing `DefinitionPlanner` and
`plan_production_definition` remain available for compatibility and other
definition kinds. Decoder and SVG definitions adapters should route pattern
planning through the explicit channel operation; there is no default fill route
or equality-based opacity fallback. `ChannelAwareProductionDecodeOperations`
provides the additive combined operation bound when an adapter needs resolver,
channel-aware definition planning and media operations together.
`ChannelAwareProductionDecodeSession` is the matching additive session contract;
its `step` receives only that explicit-channel operation set, while resume keeps
the existing job-owned mapped completion protocol.

`ChargeLedger::owner_identity` and `require_owner` provide opaque, unforgeable
same-ledger/Arc-source checks without a zero-byte identity probe.
`allocate_buffer<T: Copy>` invokes the accepted owning allocator: requested
reservation before physical allocation, actual capacity admission, honest registry
retention and physical reserve history. `LedgerBuffer` exposes checked slices,
capacity, controlled in-capacity append, truncate, atomic `replace_capacity`, and
unconditional explicit `release`. It exposes neither Vec nor lease. Copy elements
cannot own nested heap allocations; any referenced external allocations remain
# Paint channel contract API coverage

| Requirement | Public surface or behavior | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Explicit required fill/stroke planner dispatch | `PaintChannelDefinitionPlanner::plan_owned_pattern_definition` and `plan_production_pattern(..., PaintChannel, ...)` | `paint_channel_contracts.rs`: planner selects the computed `FillOpacity` or `StrokeOpacity` value explicitly |
| Preserve old API and literals | Existing `DefinitionPlanner`, `plan_production_definition`, `PatternMapping`, tickets, and pattern publication signatures are unchanged | Frozen `contracts`, `decode_publication_contracts`, `render_integration_contracts`, and `paint_publication` suites pass |
| No implicit fill/default/equality fallback | The new route always requires a channel argument; mapping opacity is returned from that channel's computed style. Missing selected property resolves to the SVG initial `1` | New test proves fill `.25`, stroke `.75`, omitted fill `1`, and omitted stroke `1` |
| Centralized validation | Both production planner entry points call `validate_production_plan`; owner/source, canonical element, style spans, bounds/transform, result kind, mapping, post operations, expansion ranges/styles/transforms, work control and cancellation are validated once | Existing production filter/mask planner and bad mapping/kind tests pass; new route uses the same validator |
| Preserve pattern channel while suspended | Existing `PatternContinuation` stores complete `PatternMapping`, `PaintChannel`, draft/request/generation, and job identity; `request_mapped` and `complete_mapped` retain and consume it | Existing `computed_pattern_mapping_transfers_same_job_pixels_and_attaches_fill_and_stroke`; new fixture completes all four channel/value cases |
| Real builder/job publication | Fixture calls channel-aware production dispatch, then `request_mapped`, writes pixels to an actual `RasterJob`, calls `complete_mapped`, and checks the returned `PatternId`, paint opacity, channel paint table, and shape attachment | `paint_channel_contracts.rs` |
| Failure, rollback, cancellation and ticket guards | Shared validator returns the existing source span and typed errors; publication preserves atomic suffix rollback and mapped ticket identity checks | Existing tests cover bad mapping/kind, source/style errors, wrong target/owner, foreign/stale ticket/job, cancellation, lower error, rollback and wrong dimensions in `decode_publication_contracts.rs` and `render_integration_contracts.rs` |
| Downstream adapter adoption | Definitions adapters implement `PaintChannelDefinitionPlanner`; decoders may use `ChannelAwareProductionDecodeOperations` and `ChannelAwareProductionDecodeSession`, whose step requires that operation set | `README.md` documents the required route and semantics. The owned definitions adapter is a read-only reference and was not changed or used for build verification. |

item.text:
Fixed both review blockers within the frozen scope. `ChannelAwareProductionDecodeOperations` now requires retained `DefinitionPlanner` capability as well as explicit-channel pattern planning. Its new dispatch functions accept the same combined trait object used by session `step`; the non-pattern route rejects `Pattern` to prevent channel-less fallback. A runtime test dispatches a Stroke pattern and a typed group filter through one `dyn ChannelAwareProductionDecodeOperations` object, then publishes the filter to its real group.

The mapped builder/job fixtures now cover eight cases: both opacities set, both omitted, fill-only `.25`, and stroke-only `.75`, each published through Fill and Stroke. Existing accepted assertions remain unchanged.

The locked offline scene check, full scene tests (153 runtime tests and two compile-fail doctests), and work-order validator all pass. Fresh logs and precise API coverage are recorded in [the repair artifacts](/Users/megasoft78/Desktop/Freelance/vexel/.cache/WO-RUST-RENDER-INTEGRATION-CONTRACTS-01/worker/artifacts/WO-RUST-PAINT-CHANNEL-CONTRACT-01/). This remains a candidate pending independent re-review, protected audit, and fresh main checks; no product acceptance is claimed.
